position: New Policy Priorities (Parental Rights in Education and Safeguarding Students)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that for K-12 systems under federal jurisdiction (D.C. public schools, Bureau of Indian Education schools and Department of Defense schools), no teacher or student be compelled to believe or adhere to race-based ideas, that no one be punished or favored by skin color, and that civil rights law add a prohibition on compelled speech. It also recommends that school staff in these systems not use a name or pronoun different from the birth record or biological sex without written parental permission, and not be required to use pronouns against their religious or moral convictions.
remaining: Enacted legislation for D.C., BIE and DoD schools barring compelled race-based belief and adding a compelled-speech prohibition to civil rights law.

Enacted legislation on name and pronoun use with written parental permission, and an employee conscience protection, applying to those systems (H.R. 2616 covers only part of this and has passed only the House).
Resolution of the Fourth Circuit appeals on DoDEA removals, which bear on the executive route.

status_summary: No law applies the recommended bans on compelled race-based belief, compelled speech or name and pronoun use specifically to D.C., BIE and DoD schools, so the stage is proposed. On 2026-05-20 the House passed H.R. 2616 (PROTECT Kids Act) 217 to 198; as reported it conditions ESEA funds on public elementary and middle schools obtaining parental consent before changing a student's gender markers, pronouns or preferred name on school forms, applies to schools generally rather than to the federal systems, has no teacher pronoun or compelled-speech provision, and the Senate received it on 2026-05-21 and referred it to its Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee, with no later action recorded. Executive Order 14190 (signed 2025-01-29) directs the Education, Defense and HHS Secretaries to deliver a strategy to end federal support for what it calls discriminatory equity ideology and social transition in K-12 schooling, without naming the three systems. DoDEA removed books and curricular materials under that and related orders from 2025-02-05; the Eastern District of Virginia enjoined further removals at five schools on 2025-10-20 and denied a motion to dismiss on 2026-03-20, with cross-appeals pending in the Fourth Circuit (covered in more detail by c04-16).

timeline.event: Executive Order 14190 was signed (published 2025-02-03); it orders an Ending Indoctrination Strategy from the Education, Defense and HHS Secretaries and defines social transition to include name or pronoun changes and discriminatory equity ideology to include blaming individuals for actions of others of the same race.

DoDEA memos directed staff to move books potentially related to gender ideology or discriminatory equity ideology out of student collections and to stop using listed curricular materials, according to the court opinion.

title: Bar compelled race-based beliefs and pronoun use in D.C., BIE and DoD schools by statute
uncertainties: The executive order does not name D.C., BIE or DoD schools and does not itself ban compelled speech or set a pronoun rule; DoDEA's book removals are about library and curricular content rather than compelled belief, so they are context and overlap c04-16. Nothing was found on Bureau of Indian Education or D.C. public school actions on these topics; a D.C.-specific bill or Interior policy may exist but was not located. H.R. 2616 applies to public elementary and middle schools receiving ESEA funds; whether that reaches BIE-funded or D.C. schools in practice was not analyzed, and DoDEA schools are not generally ESEA-funded. The court opinion refers to more than 500 books removed; the case clearinghouse cites a list of 596. Fourth Circuit briefing deadlines ran to 2026-05-13; no appellate decision was found.
